resources.string: GTL records your route on this phone only. It does not send location, IMEI, or SIM identifiers to any server. Do not interact with the app while driving. You use it at your own risk. Logging runs as a visible foreground service with a notification.
Precise location is required to start logging
Add MAPS_API_KEY to local.properties, then rebuild. OSM offline maps still work after download.

Open the system location panel to turn GPS on or choose high accuracy.
Shops, restaurants, parking, fuel from zoom 14
Rail, tram, stations, and bus stops

Parks and nature reserves. Forests stay on the base map

This removes the session and every GPS point from the phone. It cannot be undone.
This removes the downloaded OSM file from the phone. It cannot be undone.
The OSM file is missing or not a Mapsforge map. Download again, or turn off Use downloaded OSM map in Settings.

Allow location when asked. GPS and Compass update as soon as the app is open. Tap Start to record a route into SQLite on this phone, draw it on the Map, and fill the Route totals. Tap Stop to end the session. Menu → Saved tracks to delete a route, show it on the map, or share KMZ or GPX. Settings picks usage (motorbike is the default), units, and whether the last track stays on the map. Menu → Download Offline map for OSM regions or Turistautak (Hungary). Nothing is uploaded to our servers.

Settings has map and recording switches.

Use downloaded OSM map: off and disabled until you download an OSM region. When on, Map uses that Mapsforge file. Turn it off to use Google Maps on the Map tab. An OSM map section then appears in Settings: Buildings (on), POI (off — shops, restaurants, parking, fuel), Public transport (off; rail/tram/stations and bus stops), Highlight cycleways (on for Bicycle usage, off otherwise; changing usage resets this; magenta overlay from zoom 12; dedicated paths stay blue), Parks and protected areas (on), Terrain relief (off unless HGT files sit next to the .map; official Mapsforge downloads for any country usually have none). The same switches are on the Map tab layers button. Only enabled layers draw. Switching a control redraws the OSM tiles without moving the camera.

Simplify track on map: when on, only the line drawn on Map is thinned. The stored route and shared KMZ or GPX keep every accepted point.

Use GNSS only: when on, logging uses the phone satellite chip (GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou, and the rest) instead of fused location that mixes Wi-Fi, cell, and IMU. If the GPS provider is off, the app falls back to fused high accuracy.

Smooth recorded track: Kalman filter moves stored points before they are saved. The live accuracy circle stays on the raw GPS fix.

Hold still when stopped: the stored point does not wander while you are slower than the pause speed.

Show last logged route on map: after Stop, the last (or a selected) track stays on Map.

Keep whole track on the screen: while logging, each GPS refresh fits the whole track (you can still pan and zoom until the next fix).

Keep screen on while logging: while Start is on, the screen stays awake. Off by default. Idle always lets the screen sleep.

Show accuracy marker: a pale purple circle around you; its radius is the GPS accuracy in metres.

Show fix cloud: while you stand still, raw GPS fixes are dotted on the map. The outer circle is measured CEP95 in magenta. CEP stands for Circular Error Probable. The pale purple circle is still the phone’s claimed accuracy. Turning Show fix cloud on also turns on Show accuracy marker. Turning it off only hides the cloud. While you move, the cloud pauses. The log, KMZ, and GPX do not change.

Kalman smooths stored points when Smooth recorded track is on. Douglas–Peucker only thins the drawn line on Map. Run/Hike and bicycle default is GNSS only, smoothing off, every good fix, and no map simplify, so a small on-road loop stays visible. Simplify tolerance is a 1–20 m slider; lower keeps narrow loops, higher drops more vertices.

Storing points is separate from map simplify. Smart density uses speed bands from the 2014 logger (half again for Run/Hike, and half in a curve). Every good fix stores about once per min time (or sooner in a curve). Vehicles still drop points closer than 1 m; Run/Hike and bicycle drop closer than 0.5 m so a tight loop keeps vertices. If GPS bearing is missing, a heading from consecutive positions can still count as a curve.

Choosing a usage writes a full preset (GNSS only, smoothing, density, map simplify, and units). You can change any control afterwards.

Motorbike (default): metric units, GNSS only off, smooth recorded track on, mid strength, hold still when stopped, smart density, simplify on at 6 m.

Run/Hike: metric, GNSS only on (satellite chip, like a sports watch), smooth off, hold still, every good, simplify off.

Bicycle: same as Run/Hike (GNSS on, smooth off, every good, simplify off) so a slow curve or plaza loop stays on the map. If you turn simplify on, tolerance starts at 3 m.

Car matches motorbike but simplify at 8 m.

Watercraft: ICAO units (knots, nautical miles, feet), otherwise the same as car (mid strength, smart density, simplify on at 8 m).

Aircraft: ICAO units (knots, nautical miles, feet), high strength, smart density, simplify on at 15 m.

Usage type: activity type. Changing it reloads the preset, the sliders, and the units.

Units: Metric, Imperial, or ICAO on Route. Aircraft and watercraft default to ICAO; every other usage defaults to Metric. You can still pick another unit after the preset.

Map and recording switches sit in Appearance, OSM map, Recording, and Baro sections. OSM map is only shown while an OSM region is In Use (not Turistautak). Turistautak.hu is only shown while that map is In Use. Baro is only shown if this phone has a pressure sensor. Usage type and units stay at the top.

Use downloaded OSM map: off and disabled until you download an OSM region. Turn it off to show Google Maps on the Map tab.

OSM map: Buildings, POI (shops, restaurants, parking, fuel from zoom 14), Public transport (rail/tram/stations and bus stops), Highlight cycleways (magenta overlay from zoom 12; dedicated paths stay blue), Parks and protected areas, Terrain relief. Defaults: buildings and parks on; POI, public transport, and relief off; cycleways on only for Bicycle. Changing usage resets cycleways to that rule; the other OSM switches keep your last choice. Toggling a switch redraws the downloaded map. The same switches are on the Map tab layers button. Terrain relief needs HGT files next to the .map — official Mapsforge downloads for any country usually have none, so the switch stays off.

Simplify track on map: fewer vertices on Map only. When the switch is on, a 1–20 m slider (1 m steps) sets how aggressive the thinning is. KMZ, GPX, and odometer keep every stored point.

Show last logged route on map: after Stop, the last (or selected) track stays on Map.

Keep whole track on the screen: while logging, each GPS refresh fits the whole track. Pan and zoom stay allowed until the next fix.

Keep screen on while logging: while Start is on, the screen stays awake. Off by default. Idle always lets the screen sleep.

Show accuracy marker: pale purple circle; radius is GPS accuracy.

Show fix cloud: while you stand still, raw GPS fixes are dotted on the map. The outer circle is measured CEP95 in magenta (95% of those dots lie inside). CEP stands for Circular Error Probable. The pale purple circle is still the phone’s claimed accuracy at the current fix. Turning this switch on also turns on Show accuracy marker. Turning it off only hides the cloud. While you move, the cloud pauses. The log, KMZ, and GPX do not change.

Use GNSS only: satellite chip positions (all constellations) instead of fused Wi-Fi/cell/IMU. Off for vehicles. On for Run/Hike and bicycle. Falls back to fused if the GPS provider is disabled.

Smooth recorded track: Kalman moves stored points before save. The HUD accuracy circle stays on the raw GPS fix. Run/Hike and bicycle default is off so small shapes are not flattened.

Smoothing strength (when smoothing is on): continuous Low–High. Low keeps zigzag. High draws smoother arcs (aircraft).

Hold still when stopped: the stored point does not wander below the pause speed.

Recording density: continuous Smart–Every good. Smart uses speed bands. Every good stores about once per min time (or sooner in a curve). Vehicles drop stacks closer than 1 m; Run/Hike and bicycle closer than 0.5 m.

QNH: the slider is only shown if this phone has a barometer. Range 900–1100 hPa, default ISA 1013.25. Live baro and the elevation-profile dashed line use this QNH. Look up a real sea-level QNH (Qxxxx) from METAR, ATIS, or airport weather — not station pressure. Calibrate from GPS: stand still with a good GPS altitude, set QNH to METAR, tap Calibrate from GPS. That stores a pressure offset for the phone chip; it does not change the QNH slider. Reset baro clears the offset.

Auto-calibrate at start (default on, shown next to Calibrate and Reset): runs that same calculation by itself, once, as soon as two consecutive GPS fixes after Start (each passing the accuracy/satellite filter) agree on altitude within 15 m, so the offset matches the day’s real weather without you standing still and tapping Calibrate first. Requiring two fixes to agree avoids locking onto a single glitchy altitude reading, which single fixes right after a location request starts sometimes are. Calibrate from GPS and Reset baro are still there and still useful with Auto-calibrate on: Auto-calibrate only fires during a recording, so tap Calibrate yourself first if you want accurate baro on the GPS tab before pressing Start; tap it again mid-ride if that first fix turned out to have a mediocre altitude, since Auto-calibrate does not retry once it has set the offset; and Reset baro is the only way back to raw ISA 1013.25, which Auto-calibrate never does on its own. With Auto-calibrate off, Calibrate from GPS and Reset baro are the only way to set or clear the offset at all. GPS altitude is independent. IGC pressure altitude (later export) would use 1013.25, not this slider.

Live satellite counts (GPS L1/L5, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou, QZSS, NavIC), SNR quality, latitude, longitude, accuracy, and altitude. Provider sits in the constellation strip to the right of NavIC (short names: GPS, Fused, NET). The altitude card is labelled GPS / Baro: GPS altitude (MSL when Android provides it, then GNSS, then fused), a slash, then barometric altitude from Settings QNH and the optional GPS calibration offset (or — if this phone has no pressure sample). Logging status and ambient temperature are on the Route tab. Altitude prefers Mean Sea Level when Android provides it, then the GNSS chip ellipsoid height, then fused. Values below the Dead Sea or above typical flight level are treated as missing (fused on some phones reports about −1800 m). While logging, Kalman can smooth stored points if Smooth recorded track is on; the HUD lat/lon and accuracy circle stay on the raw location. Use GNSS only takes that raw location from the satellite chip instead of fused location. Smart density still uses the 2014 speed bands.

A polar skyplot sits under SNR. Centre is the zenith; the outer ring is the horizon; inner rings are 30° and 60° elevation. Twelve o’clock is north. Colour is the constellation. A filled disk is used in the fix; a hollow ring is in view only. An inner ring means an L5-class carrier. Dual-frequency L1+L5 of the same satellite is one point. The plot updates without Start and is not stored in the log.

When Show fix cloud is on, the GPS tab adds four numbers from the same raw fixes: n is how many points are in the sliding window (at most 120 points or 120 seconds). RMS is the root-mean-square distance of those points from their own centroid, in metres — one number for how spread the cloud is. CEP95 is the radius of the circle around that centroid that contains 95% of the points; it is measured scatter, not the pale purple claimed-accuracy circle. CEP stands for Circular Error Probable. Reported is the median of positive accuracy values in the window (the chip’s claim), so you can compare claim vs measurement. Turning Show fix cloud on also turns on Show accuracy marker. CEP95 is omitted until n is at least 8. The cloud is only valid while you stand; walking stretches it into a trail.

Session totals after Start, and for a saved or last session: elapsed time, odometer, time moving, time waiting, altitude, bearing, logging status, ambient temperature (hardware sensor, or 0 if this phone has none), lean angle (phone flat on a motorbike tank), temperature range when the sensor exists, and a GPS elevation profile (dashed barometric line when pressure samples exist). Speed and average speed are 0 while Idle; after Start they follow live GPS speed and the session average. Axis min/max is GPS and baro together, at least 50 m, so a few metres of GPS noise does not fill the plot. The legend shows the last GPS and baro values. Baro uses Settings QNH and the optional GPS calibration offset.

Centers on your current location when you open the tab. Idle, you can pan away; the map does not snap back. After Start it follows you and draws the recorded track. A My location button (top left: cyan GPS crosshair, same circle as the broom) recenters on the GPS fix without changing zoom. A HUD over Google Maps and OSM shows large speed (units from Settings), accuracy in metres, and GNSS used/in view as used/in-view. While logging it also shows odometer, elapsed time, and a pulsing REC. Idle with a GPS fix: a dim compact panel at the bottom left (same speed, accuracy, GNSS). Hidden when a saved track is on the map and you are not logging. The Map HUD does not show altitude; GPS / Baro is on the GPS tab, Route totals use GPS altitude, and the dashed profile line is QNH baro. Kalman smooths stored points only if Smooth recorded track is on; Simplify only thins the drawn line. A pale purple circle around you is the GPS accuracy (radius equals the accuracy in metres). Turn it off in Settings. A small red usage silhouette (aircraft, boat, car, motorbike, bicycle, or Run/Hike) marks your position and stays upright in portrait. A live GPS fix sits on a cyan GNSS reticle. A north marker stays on the map. On Google Maps, a layers button left of zoom picks Map, Satellite, Hybrid, or Terrain; the choice is remembered. On a downloaded OSM map, the same button opens the OSM layer switches (also in Settings → OSM map): buildings, POI (shops, restaurants, parking, fuel from zoom 14), public transport including bus stops, magenta cycleway highlight from zoom 12, parks, terrain. Terrain relief stays off unless HGT files sit next to the .map. Show fix cloud: while you stand still, raw GPS fixes are dotted on the map. The outer circle is measured CEP95 in magenta (95% of those dots lie inside). CEP stands for Circular Error Probable. The pale purple circle is still the phone’s claimed accuracy at the current fix. Turning Show fix cloud on also turns on Show accuracy marker. Turning it off only hides the cloud. While you move, the cloud pauses. The log and KMZ do not change. With “Show last logged route on map” a saved track stays visible. “Keep whole track on the screen” fits the whole route after each GPS refresh while logging. Saved tracks → Show on map opens that session here, switches Settings to that session’s usage, and draws it with those settings. After that, changing usage or sliders redraws the same log that way. A broom button at the top left takes that line off the map without deleting the log. Below it, My location recenters on you. A green S marks the start of the drawn track; a red E marks the end when you are not logging (while logging the usage silhouette is now).

Tap a point on Google, OSM, or Turistautak. Drag and zoom stay. The menu offers Distance and GPS coordinate. Distance sets that point as the target. The straight line updates on the HUD on every live GPS fix, including when you move away (D2.7km; miles or NM from Settings). A small compass on that row points at the point. Straight up means it is ahead. While you move, the needle follows your GPS course. While you stand still, it uses the compass, and the top of the phone is forward. Within about 20 m, or inside the GPS accuracy, the needle hides and the distance stays. Tap the row to clear both. GPS coordinate stacks longitude and latitude on a card. Copy puts latitude, longitude on the clipboard so a map search can find the point. Address stays hidden: these maps do not return a full address.

Search (magnifying glass under My location) is only there while an OSM or Turistautak map is in use. Type at least 3 characters. Up to 5 matches from that map, the closest good name first: city, village, statue, house, and other named places. Tap a row. Yes centers the map on it and shows the straight-line distance on the HUD. The same pointer appears for that target. No leaves the map as it is. My location follows you again.
These switches apply when a downloaded OSM region is on Map. They do not change Google Maps.
Buildings — on. Fills building footprints. Turn off if the map is too busy in town.
POI — off. Shops, restaurants, parking, fuel from zoom 14. Not bus stops.
Public transport — off. Rail, tram, stations, and bus stops.
Highlight cycleways — on for Bicycle usage, off otherwise. Magenta overlay from zoom 12. Dedicated cycleways stay blue. Changing usage resets this. On-road lanes are not in official Mapsforge files.
Parks and protected areas — on. Parks and nature reserves. Forests stay on the base map.
Terrain relief — off until HGT elevation files sit next to the map or in hills/. Official Mapsforge downloads usually have none.

The Compass tab shows heading from the phone’s rotation sensor. MAG is magnetic north (the sensor). TRUE is geographic north: magnetic heading plus declination from the last GPS fix. Switch MAG or TRUE on this tab, not in Settings; it is not tied to usage. Default is MAG. TRUE needs a GPS fix; without one the dial stays MAG and shows No GPS. If sensor accuracy is low, a warning under the dial asks you to draw a figure-8 in the air — the chip calibrates itself, there is no offset slider. Works without Start.

Saved tracks → select one or more sessions → Share selected → KMZ or GPX.

KMZ is for Google Earth (KML plus play, pause, and stop icons). If Google Earth is not installed, get it from Play Store, then open the shared file. Tap an icon on the map for that point’s details. The visible line is draped on the terrain (height 0) so it stays on the road at close zoom. Icons sit on the same coordinates: Start at the first path point, Pause on the track, Stop at the last stored point. Re-share KMZ after this app update; older files still float beside the road when you zoom in.

Start: UTC datetime YYYY:MM:DD HH:MM:SS, then temp= in the selected unit (temp=N/A if the phone has no sample), GPS lon then lat, Altitude: (GPS) and Baro: (barometer at the current Settings QNH and GPS calibration offset, or Baro: -) in the selected unit. No Speed, Avg. Speed, Max speed, duration, distance, usage, or lean.

Pause: title Pause. The same datetime, temp, lon/lat, Altitude, and Baro, plus Speed: (instantaneous GPS speed at that pause, selected unit), duration= from Start (seconds if 60 s or less, whole minutes under 60 min, otherwise HH:MM:SS), and distance= so far in the selected unit. No Avg. Speed or Max speed. Standing pauses collapse to one icon; a pause on top of Start or Stop is omitted so Stop details are not titled Pause.

Stop: title Stop. The same datetime, temp, lon/lat, Altitude, and Baro, plus Avg. Speed: and Max speed: from the session path (selected unit, one decimal), then duration= and distance= for the full session. No instant Speed. Units: metric km/h, m/km, °C; imperial mph, ft/mi, °F; ICAO kt, ft/NM, °C.

The Google Earth track also keeps speed, cumulative distance in metres, GPS altitude, and baro (metres at the current Settings QNH and offset) as ExtendedData. GPX elevation stays GPS.

GPX 1.1 is for OsmAnd, Komoot, Garmin Connect, Relive, QGIS, and other apps. Each session is one track with one segment. Points have latitude, longitude, GPS elevation, and UTC time. Start, Pause, and Stop are waypoints on the same path points as KMZ. Several selected sessions become one file with several tracks. Filename GTL_yyyyMMdd_HHmmss.gpx.

resources.string: The cloud is the last two minutes of raw GPS fixes.
The cloud pauses while you move.
Waiting for a GNSS fix. In a tunnel this drops to Poor.
No account, no ads, no IMEI, no remote tracking.
The Map tab can optionally show OpenStreetMap data from a file you download on the phone. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, licensed under the Open Database License (ODbL).
